title: Desk Guidance on the Chronic-Outage Credit Load Factor for High-Demand and Three-Phase Electric Service Agreements
content:
The care center applies the following rule to the chronic-outage credit on an **Electric Service Agreement** whose premise carries a large load.

**Rule.** The chronic credit amount is multiplied by a load factor of 1.5 when the highest measured demand on the agreement's bills is 20 kW or more and the meter in service at the premise is an AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter, by 1.25 when exactly one of those two holds, and by 1 when neither holds, and the product is rounded to the cent.

**What is read.**
- The highest measured demand on the agreement's bills: the largest measured demand in kW shown on any bill of the agreement.
- The meter in service at the premise, from the customer's **Metering Service** records: whether its meter type is the AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter.

**Truth table.**

| Highest measured demand 20 kW or more | AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter in service | Load factor |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 1.5 |
| yes | no | 1.25 |
| no | yes | 1.25 |
| no | no | 1, no load adjustment |

A highest measured demand of exactly 20 kW is 20 kW or more; one of 19.9 kW is not.

**Where the load factor acts.** It multiplies the chronic credit amount, and the product is rounded to the cent at that point.

**Hypothetical figures.**

| Chronic credit amount | Load factor | Product rounded to the cent |
|---|---|---|
| $30.00 | 1.5 | $45.00 |
| $25.00 | 1.25 | $31.25 |
| $17.50 | 1.25 | $21.88 (from 21.875) |
| $30.00 | 1 | $30.00 |
